_doc: Engine Capability Map. Each capability is [id, name, owner-skill, maturity, contributors?]. Maturity: E=established production, M=emerging production, X=experimental research, S=speculative. Exactly one owner per capability; contributors must coordinate through the owner's contract.

areas.name: Requirements & configuration profiles
caps: Translate prioritized requirements (C-PROD) into profiles, tiers and non-goals
Engine configuration profiles & feature sets (indie 2D → AAA open-world online)
Hardware tier definitions (the only definition of tier names) incl. server instance classes and refresh-rate classes
Platform matrix (OS × ISA × API; store axis from PLAT.SVC.pc-storefronts, platform-console entries and BLD.REL.store-variants) generated from skills.json platform_variants and implementer variants

areas.name: Structure & boundaries
caps: Subsystem replaceability & optionality (modules absent in small profiles)
Global conventions: units, handedness, up-axis, coordinate spaces
Cross-domain arbitration & escalation of boundary disputes
Registered platform backend slots (RHI, IO, audio endpoint, input, sockets, crash, save storage, service SDK, IME/a11y bridge)
Registration policy: what must self-register (phases, render features, services, cvars, codegen inputs) and the ban on central tables (mechanism in C-MOD)
Contract binding policy: implementation chosen at compile/link/load time; batch-granular interfaces; no per-item virtual dispatch across contracts on hot paths

areas.name: Architecture governance
caps: ADR lifecycle with evidence, alternatives, revisit conditions
Automated architectural fitness functions (layering, dependency, contract conformance)
Anti-legacy review against the flagged-pattern catalogue (data/legacy-patterns.json)
Technology radar (data/radar.json): maturity, owners, revisit triggers, non-goals
Governance weight per organization tier (consumes tier names from ARCH.ORG.staffing)

Maturity-class transitions: radar review at every milestone exit, promotion checklist (evidence, profile retag, optional-to-required change, extension-tier freeze, conformance, budget) and demotion into legacy-patterns on vendor withdrawal

areas.name: Research & evidence
caps: Prototype/spike protocol producing evidence where literature is thin
Source policy for agents: allowed, cite-only and forbidden source classes, clean-room separation of reading and implementing agents

areas.name: Agent organization
caps: Milestone → work-package decomposition by workstream (intra-subtree decomposition in ARCH.ORG.delegated-planning)
Milestone ladder with per-milestone skill set, contract maturity & exit criteria (data/milestones.json)
Agent staffing tiers (small 3 agents, mid 8, large 16; data/organizations.json) co-hosting skills by workstream; sole owner of tier names

Escalation tiers & decision SLAs; a non-party lead of the workstream is the first-instance arbiter of intra-workstream disputes; engine-architect decides cross-workstream disputes and disputes in which the arbitrating lead is a party

Register of decisions requiring human authorization (contracts, spend, NDA material, and irreversible live-production actions: player-data restore/edit, GM/admin commands on shipping servers, ban waves, rollout promotion past canary, global kill switch and remote-config changes, economy grants)
Program risk register & risk-driven milestone ordering
Failure attribution & routing policy, revert-first (bisection engine in BLD.CI.bisection)

Critic calibration via seeded defects at every stage (G1, G2, S1–S4 canary defects in sampled changes); recall and precision tracked per critic; below-threshold critics stop counting as gates; a below-threshold critic blocks the stages in its scope (fail closed) until a recalibrated or replacement critic passes its canaries, with interim sign-off recorded under ARCH.ORG.human-gates
Independent adjudication of rejected and partially accepted findings
Per-change agent/model/task attestation in the ledger

Independence matrix: never-same-agent pairs (decider vs governance reviewer, implementer vs oracle author, builder vs adjudicator, security reviewer vs reviewed code, milestone owner vs gate owner) enforced by staffing at every organization tier; co-hosting capped by capability count
Skill-library lifecycle during the build: territory re-bounding by ADR, check.py re-gate, SKILL.md regeneration, agent re-brief, library versioning tied to C-RELEASE; review at every milestone exit
Program cost ledger: agent compute per skill/milestone, CI/device-farm/cloud-cook cost, load-test hosting, server cost per CCU
Human sampling of adjudications and S3/S4 pass verdicts at a fixed rate

Sensitive write sets (registry parsers, crypto, auth, sandboxes, build & CI) require a K-SEC gate plus a second agent's approval; the agent control plane (ledger, access classes, critics.json, check.py, registry, human-gates register, seeds) needs human-gate approval and a fitness function diffs it against the protected branch
Agent continuity: lock leases with heartbeats and fencing tokens, stale-lock reclamation, mandatory task hand-off record and re-brief when an agent crashes, runs out of context or is replaced
Delegated planning: program-orchestration issues per-lead work packages and cross-workstream integration tasks; leads decompose inside their subtree (work-package format in C-ORCH)

Model/prompt lineage and requalification: implementer, oracle author and S3/S4 critics use different model families or versions (otherwise the human-audit rate rises); any change of agent model or prompt re-runs seeded-defect calibration and holdouts before the agent counts as a gate; the model is recorded in provenance
Scope control: budget envelope per milestone, burn/slip trigger, ordered descope list (configurations and non-goals), stop/cancel criterion, human gate for envelope raise

Human capacity model: role roster, SLA per gate class, non-blocking continuation (gated task parks, agents proceed on independent work packages), batching cadence per milestone, delegate/expiry rule, gate-wait-time metric; creator-panel sampling per discipline (task completion, time-to-first-asset)

External lead-time register (platform-holder admission and NDAs, devkit procurement, certification queue slots, pen-test booking, middleware negotiation) with start-by dates derived from milestone exits, feeding ARCH.ORG.risk

areas.name: Engine product management
caps: Game-team bug & feature intake and triage SLAs
Customer/reference project corpus validating each release
Engine licensing & terms model for game teams
Cross-title crash, performance and developer-experience metrics feeding the roadmap
Intake of licensee patches with IP terms
Legal and privacy basis of vendor-bound telemetry: licensee-controlled opt-in, controller/processor roles, DPA template, allowed data classes, no silent billing telemetry

areas.name: Platform abstraction layer
caps: OS services abstraction (VM, files, time, dynamic libraries)
CPU topology & feature discovery (hybrid cores, SMT, caches, NUMA, ISA)
Platform capability feature query (tier names from ARCH.REQ.hardware-tiers)
Cloud-streaming policy (session detection, latency budget, device-kind changes); platform work in PLAT.CON/DESK.cloud-streaming
Bootstrap base (C-BASE): raw allocator, raw sinks, hook tables
Thread creation, affinity & QoS per OS
Thread-affinity registry & isolation of OS-thread-bound APIs behind queues; engine loop never assumes the OS main thread
Processes, pipes, shared memory, local/dev sockets, HTTP(S)/TLS client (platform stacks)
System events & queries: memory pressure, reachability, audio endpoints, locale, OS accessibility settings, overlay/focus, storage, page size
Device capability database (single store): device records, driver deny-lists, hardware → tier keys, remote updates
Supported OS versions, deprecation & beta-OS validation
NDA platform extensions: segregated modules/repos, public stubs, sanitized CI results, access classes
Display enumeration, modes, DPI, HDR & VRR capability, dynamic HDR/EDR headroom events
Lifecycle & system-event injection (suspend/resume, constrained mode, sign-out, controller disconnect, memory pressure, thermal)
Cursor management (hardware/software cursors, confinement, relative mode), clipboard, file dialogs, drag-and-drop
Target-platform tooling contract content: cook format variants, shader-target hook, packager hook, deploy/run/debug
Engine as cloud render host: headless GPU rendering, frame capture, low-latency hardware encode, video/input back-channel, multi-tenant GPU packing

areas.name: Desktop & handheld PC
caps: OS security interplay (Defender scanning, controlled folders, notarization, TCC, sandboxes, anti-cheat on Proton)
Windows on ARM (ARM64EC, emulation interop, middleware availability)
PAL implementation for Windows/Linux/SteamOS/macOS (C-PAL backend: OS services, windowing, threads, clocks, IO, display, power, events)
PC-build cloud streaming (touch-overlay controls, UI-scale tier)
Target-platform cook variants, shader-target and packager hooks, deploy/run/debug

areas.name: Console-class platforms
caps: Console OS & memory model (UMA, reserved memory, fixed hardware)
PAL implementation for console OS (C-PAL backend: OS services, windowing, threads, clocks, IO, display, power, events)

Confidential implementations of registered slots (IO/decompression units, audio endpoints, save storage, crash upload, system keyboard/IME/TTS bridge, entitlement SDK, console pad & adaptive-trigger libraries, sockets/relay, console XR SDK) behind public interfaces owned by domain skills
Target-platform cook variants, shader-target and packager hooks, deploy/run/debug
Console first-party trophies/achievements, privileges and parental controls behind the public C-SVC interface
Console first-party entitlements, presence and activities behind the public C-SVC interface
Console packaging and signing tools (confidential, per platform holder; public stubs on BLD.REL.packaging/submission)
Console submission validators and pre-submission checkers (confidential, per platform holder; public stubs on BLD.REL.packaging/submission)
Console mandated patch/DLC formats and size rules (confidential, per platform holder; public stubs on BLD.REL.packaging/submission)
Console devkit CI lanes (confidential, per platform holder; public stubs on BLD.REL.packaging/submission)
Public conformance-passing null implementation of every confidential slot so non-cleared agents run the same suites

areas.name: Mobile & portable
caps: Mobile thermal/power signal backends (ADPF thermal headroom, performance-hint sessions, iOS thermal state) feeding CORE.SCALE.governor; no independent control loop
Runtime storage constraints (free-space checks, OS cache purge)
Mobile present-rate/pacing backends implementing C-PRESENT/C-PAL (selection policy in CORE.SCALE.actuators)
PAL implementation for iOS/Android/visionOS (C-PAL backend: OS services, windowing, threads, clocks, IO, display, power, events)
Resizable/multi-window mobile apps (iPadOS windowing, foldable posture, ChromeOS/desktop modes)
Device geolocation: fused location, geofences, background/approximate permissions, battery policy, location privacy class
Target-platform cook variants, shader-target and packager hooks, deploy/run/debug

areas.name: Platform & online services integration
caps: User identity, sign-in, account linking, crossplay identity
Privileges & parental controls at feature boundaries
Age verification, playtime/spending limits & regional policy enforcement
Voice & text chat end to end: path selection (service vs game transport), channels, privileges, mute/block
Remote generative-AI/inference boundary (auth, quotas, cost, latency, routing)
Platform-user model: user handle, sign-in/out & user-change events, primary-user rules, guests (all platforms)
Cross-platform friends, parties, presence & invites via backend; reconciliation with first-party social, privileges and blocks
Voice reporting capture & retention for moderation
First-party service emulation for C-SVC (identity, entitlements, privileges, achievements)
Demo & time-limited trial SKUs with entitlement gating & save carry-over
Secure client token storage and system-browser/PKCE login with account linking
PC storefront SDK adapters (Steamworks, Epic Online Services, GOG Galaxy, Microsoft Store/GDK-PC), Steam Input and overlay rules

areas.name: XR
caps: Scene understanding (planes, meshes, semantic labels, environment depth)
XR runtime backends: OpenXR, visionOS Compositor Services (console XR SDK slot in PLAT.CON.confidential-slots)
OS-composited shared-space scenes (engine exports a scene description via C-RSCENE change streams)
Body, face & eye-expression tracking inputs (OpenXR extensions) with biometric privacy class
XR authoring: play-in-headset, device simulator, in-headset editing, passthrough/anchor/scene-mesh preview

areas.name: Web platform
caps: WASM threads, cross-origin isolation, no-threads fallback & memory limits
PAL implementation for browser (WASM) (C-PAL backend: OS services, windowing, threads, clocks, IO, display, power, events)
std3d-class web tier gated by C-GPUTIER (bindless, memory64)
Browser-capability share measurement (WebGPU, threads, memory) from web analytics and portal SDKs
Target-platform cook variants, shader-target and packager hooks, deploy/run/debug

areas.name: Live operations
caps: Live-title SLOs over engine telemetry, alerting hooks, operational incident runbooks & launch-readiness review
Player-support data inspection & restoration boundary over NET.SRV.persistence (audited)

areas.name: Commerce & monetization boundary
caps: Consumable, non-consumable & subscription purchases via first-party stores
Server-side receipt/entitlement verification boundary (client only forwards receipts; grants via NET.SRV.transactions)
Randomized-item odds disclosure & regional spending rules
Ad-SDK integration boundary (consent, mediation, rewarded callbacks, isolation)
Refund, void and chargeback revocation with clawback of granted entitlements

areas.name: Server host platform
caps: PAL implementation for server hosts (C-PAL backend)
Server host OS & container specifics (Linux, ARM64 hosts, huge pages)
Target-platform cook variants, shader-target and packager hooks, deploy/run/debug

areas.name: Lifecycle, modules, configuration, errors
caps: Parallel boot via init dependency graph
Service registry & dependency-injection policy (no hidden globals)
Layered configuration, cvars, command line, per-platform/device and remote layers with precedence
Error-handling & failure model (expected-style results, fatal vs recoverable)
Assertion tiers & contract checks (C++26 contracts as adoption path)
Implementation language(s) ADR (C++, Rust or mixed), standard baseline & compiler feature policy, coding standard; ADR criteria include agent-verifiability and undefined-behaviour class exposure
Serial bootstrap phase until the scheduler is live; hand-off to parallel init
Engine-wide ownership & cross-thread reference rules (policy; retirement service implemented in CORE.CONC.retirement)
Engine IPC/RPC transport & process model for tools, workers, crash handler, profiler
Config reads via immutable snapshots latched at sync points; queued change notification
Multi-language interop & memory-safe components (FFI/ABI rules, ownership across boundaries)
Config trust tiers per layer & per-cvar settable-from allow-lists (no code loading or path cvars from command-line, intent or remote layers in shipping)

areas.name: Math & numerics
caps: Double & mixed-precision math for large worlds
Random numbers (counter-based / per-stream for parallel determinism) & noise
Wide-SIMD / SPMD kernels for fixed and scalable (VLA) vector ISAs, runtime ISA dispatch
Large-magnitude/arbitrary-precision numeric types with canonical serialization
Fixed-point numerics for cross-platform lockstep and rollback

areas.name: Memory
caps: Virtual memory reservation, mapping & page-size policy (4K/64K/2M, large/huge pages, commit/decommit granularity per platform, client and server)
Allocator family with scoped arenas: reset keyed to a completion token or frame-in-flight slot (C-LIFETIME), pools, thread caches
Memory debugging (guard pages, poisoning, sanitizer integration)
Unified-memory CPU/GPU accounting, reported into RES.MGMT.arbitration (no independent arbitration)
Field detection of heap corruption in shipping builds: sampled guard allocator (E) and hardware memory-tagging mode (M), overhead budgets in C-BUDGET

areas.name: Core types & containers
caps: Containers (arrays, open-addressing hash maps, inline, SoA, intrusive, rings)
Non-cryptographic & stable content hashing with versioned algorithm/seed guarantees
Compression codec library for all users (package and non-package): vetted zstd/LZ4/Kraken-class decoders, SIMD tuning, fuzz registration
Vetted cryptographic primitives wrapper, CSPRNG, per-platform selection
Keyed hashing (SipHash class) mandated for containers keyed by untrusted data

areas.name: Concurrency primitives
caps: Synchronization primitives (futex-backed locks, events, spin with backoff); no subsystem-wide locks on frame paths; priority inheritance/donation where the OS offers it, no spinning across QoS classes, lock-class registry (frame-critical, RT-forbidden)
Lock-free / wait-free structures (MPMC queues, work-stealing deques)
Thread-safety annotations and model-checking hooks (litmus/linearizability reference scenes and threshold proposals only; suite authorship belongs to the contract's oracle_author)
Retirement service (C-LIFETIME): completion-token, fence and epoch retire queues shared with safe memory reclamation
Cross-thread data layout: per-target destructive-interference size, padding and sharding rules, per-worker sharded counters and queues, padding lint

areas.name: Jobs, task graphs, fibers
caps: Fibers & language coroutines (fiber-safe TLS, debugger/profiler/sanitizer annotations)
IO & GPU completion integration into the scheduler

Engine thread inventory (sole authority on which threads exist), core reservation, OS priority/QoS mapping, real-time thread rules, middleware pool adapters, oversubscription detection; forbidden-primitive lint for real-time threads
Serial/deterministic execution mode & seeded schedule perturbation hooks
Task tracing, critical-path & utilization analysis, OS scheduler correlation
Dependency-race detection for declared task dependencies
Shipping inline/cooperative mode: the same task graph on 0–2 workers, no blocking waits on host threads, yield to the host event loop
Task cancellation: stop tokens, propagation to dependents, cancelling in-flight IO/GPU work, cancel-vs-completion and cancel-vs-retire ordering

areas.name: Frame & time orchestration
caps: Frame pipelining & frames in flight (incl. whether any dedicated render/RHI thread exists, by ADR)
Tick phases & the minimal set of named global sync points (each justified by ADR); ordering otherwise derived from C-FRAME access declarations
Fixed-step simulation with interpolation; bounded catch-up (max substeps, dilation vs drop) with cadence fixed for lockstep
Time domains (real, game, dilation, pause) & clocks
Input-to-photon latency & frame pacing (Reflex / Anti-Lag class)
Unified access declarations for all phase work (ECS systems and service resources); the single frame scheduler that compiles the per-frame graph and resolves conflicts across and inside phases
Canonical simulation dependency order (partial order over declared access; total order only where C-DET requires it)
Time-sliced / rate-bucketed ticking & per-phase tick budgets
Detection of writes to data owned by another phase
Present timeline, pacing feedback & interposed presenters (C-PRESENT)
Host-driven frame entry (requestAnimationFrame, display link, Choreographer, xrWaitFrame) with a non-blocking cooperative frame step

Concurrent per-world frame graphs on one worker pool: independent time domains and cadences, cross-world priority and fair share, per-world overload isolation, process-global vs world-scoped sync points
Per-entity and per-team time scale (hit-stop, bullet-time on a subset) obeyed by animation, physics, VFX, audio, abilities and movement; deterministic and recorded

areas.name: Object model & identity
caps: Hybrid object-model policy (ECS vs services vs asset objects vs UI objects)
Reference kinds & explicit lifetime (owner + generational handles; no tracing GC over engine objects; script references are weak handles)
Events & messaging: deferred, batched delivery at declared consumption points by default
Multiple isolated world instances per process; world-scoped state reachable only through a world handle; no current-world global

areas.name: Entity component system
caps: Component storage (archetype chunks vs sparse sets)
Lowering ECS systems into the frame access model (no separate ECS scheduler)
ECS ↔ subsystem bulk-sync adapters (physics, animation, audio, render, transforms)
World/component snapshot & restore, rollback-able component marking
Debug declared-vs-actual access checking & system-order ambiguity detection

areas.name: Reflection & metadata
caps: Reflection generation (codegen now; C++26 static reflection when available)
Static/compile-time reflection & resolved IDs on runtime paths; string lookup only at tool, script and serialization boundaries
State classes on reflected properties (transient, derived, saved, replicated, predicted, persisted, stripped from shipping) declared once; registries derive from them

areas.name: Serialization & schema
caps: Serializable command/transaction core (schema, apply/invert, journal, merge hooks)

areas.name: Runtime scalability
caps: Device-profile application & per-context knob sets (active view count/split-screen, XR) & scalability knob registry
Closed-loop runtime performance/power governor (C-GOVERN module; shipping-grade inputs)
Actuator registry (frame-rate cap/refresh selection, dynres, significance, VFX, animation rate, worker count & P/E placement)
Startup crash-loop detection and safe-mode boot: crash marker, N-strike rollback of settings to last-known-good, plugin/mod disable

areas.name: Runtime resource management
caps: Dependency-aware loading; soft references, budgeted dependency-aware loading
Fully asynchronous loading: no blocking waits on frame-critical tasks or host/OS-bound threads; completions via C-TASK tokens
Cross-pool memory & IO-bandwidth arbitration (textures, geometry pages, shadow pages, audio, animation, world cells, BVH, model weights); single physical budget on UMA; OS pressure signals
Batched GPU-originated streaming requests (feedback buffers) & latency contract
Staged load pipeline, per-stage queues, staging-memory budget, batching, cancellation

Streaming-correctness oracle: no required cell missing at traversal speed, residency invariants under arbitration (hooks, reference scenes and threshold proposals only; suite authorship belongs to the contract's oracle_author)

areas.name: Asynchronous IO
caps: Async IO backends (io_uring, IOCP, DirectStorage; console variants via PLAT.CON.confidential-slots)
IO scheduling, prioritization, queue depth, batching
Memory-mapped IO restricted to prefetched/locked or tool-side use
CPU decompression as an IO stage (scheduling only; codecs in CORE.TYPES.codecs)
HTTP/CDN IO backend with persistent content cache, prefetch & offline policy
Durable write primitives: write queues and coalescing, durability classes (fsync/F_FULLFSYNC, directory sync), atomic replace, quota and disk-full errors, read-deadline protection

areas.name: Packages & virtual file system
caps: Compression codec selection per package (implementations in CORE.TYPES.codecs)
VFS mounting & layering (base, patch, DLC, mods)
Access-order package layout from load/stream traces (co-location, request coalescing), validated by PRF.LOAD.load-time

areas.name: Asset identity & registry
caps: Asset registry & queries; cooked, chunked, on-demand registry with streamed indexes and an incremental editor registry (never a full scan or residency at boot)
Asset rights/license/provenance metadata through cook to a shipping rights manifest

areas.name: Import & interchange
caps: Texture source formats (EXR, PNG, TIFF, PSD)

areas.name: Cooking & derived data
caps: Cook-step processor contract (inputs, cache keys, determinism)
Texture processing & GPU texture-compression encoding (BCn, ASTC)
World-scoped derived-data build graph: region invalidation, distributed bakes, staleness reporting
On-demand cooking, cook-server streaming to running targets, play without full cook
GPU & training cook steps with pinned-artifact determinism & dataset lineage
Image processing (mips, normal maps, channel packing)
Mesh boolean, remesh & UV-unwrap operations for processors and blockout
ML-assisted retopology/UV/LOD techniques as processor options
Incremental cook equals clean cook (bit/tolerance per determinism class)
Multi-site derived-data cache fleet (replication, eviction, cost)
Video transcode cook (codec/bitrate ladder, muxed tracks, HDR metadata)

areas.name: Content validation
caps: Content budget validation (triangles, texture sizes, bones)
Asset reference, size & chunk auditing tools
Validate-on-save & pre-submit content checks (domain validators registered via hooks)

areas.name: World model
caps: World representation strategy (data-oriented, no universal scene graph)
One-file-per-object layout for collaboration; with semantic merge
Async non-blocking whole-unit load with loading-screen hand-off (minimal/2D default)

areas.name: Partitioning & streaming
caps: HLOD strategy & generation orchestration (builder implemented as a C-COOK world-scope processor; invalidation and distribution belong to CNT.COOK.world-build)
Budgeted, time-sliced cell activation with bulk registration

areas.name: Transforms & spatial queries
caps: Generic spatial index & query service for non-physics consumers
Spatial hashing for massive agent counts
View registry & arbitration, view origin, listener/streaming-source derivation (C-VIEW)
Per-phase transform change sets published once to all spatial replicas

areas.name: Environment systems
caps: Water query service (C-ENV provider: height, velocity, depth, body id)
Global wind field state & queries (via C-ENV)
Interactive shallow-water / heightfield water simulation (local surface waves, wakes, flooding)
Single participating-media integrator: froxel/grid injection, heterogeneous sparse volumes, composition order with fog and translucency (vfx and fluids inject via C-ATMOS)
Terrain in ray tracing and SDF scenes: heightfield/clipmap to BLAS or SDF proxy

areas.name: Procedural generation
caps: Road/rail network generation: terrain conforming, intersections, lane-graph export

areas.name: Voxel worlds
caps: Runtime world edits with replication & persistence hand-off
Voxel world generation at chunk stream-in (via C-PCG)

areas.name: Render architecture
caps: Shading path choice (forward+, deferred, visibility buffer)
Simulation→render extraction: change-tracked, parallel, versioned delta streams (CPU cost O(changes))

Multi-view rendering: split-screen, PiP, captures, stereo/multiview; isolated preview scenes with their own lighting and budget for 3D UI and render-to-texture cameras; UI-less, HDR and tiled capture honoring platform capture restrictions (PLAT.SVC.capture)
Submission strategy per hardware tier (GPU-driven vs CPU-culled batched), by ADR; TBDR suitability
Editor render features: GPU picking, selection outline, editor primitives
Per-view scene-texture layout & producer phases per shading path (C-SCENETEX)
Lighting-environment block & its early-phase publication (C-LIGHTENV; static default without atmosphere)
Render-cache invalidation channel: GPU-deforming instance flags, dirty-region/page invalidation (shadow pages, surface caches), BLAS update requests
Portal views with recursive rendering and spatial-query transform through portals
Spanned multi-display output with per-display off-axis projection and bezel correction
Depth and projection conventions (reverse-Z, float depth, infinite far plane, clip-space jitter, pixel-centre and Y-flip differences across D3D/Vulkan/Metal/WebGPU), referenced by C-SCENETEX
Genlock/frame-lock cluster rendering for virtual production

areas.name: Hardware interface
caps: Pipeline-state models & caches (PSO, pipeline libraries, shader objects), async creation
GPU fault instrumentation: breadcrumbs, markers, dump generation, device-lost recovery
Binding-model tiers: bindless (default where capable) and bounded bind-group/descriptor-set tier
Implicit-synchronization backends (WebGPU): graph barrier output mapped or elided
Driver policy rules evaluated against C-PAL device records (no own deny-list)
Null/software GPU device for headless CI (WARP/lavapipe/SwiftShader class)
GPU-generated work primitives (indirect, device-generated commands, backing memory)
Backend conformance test suite (hooks only; suite authorship belongs to the contract's oracle_author)
D3D12 backend: validation layers & conformance runs
Vulkan backend: validation layers & conformance runs
Metal backend: validation layers & conformance runs
WebGPU backend: validation layers & conformance runs
Work-graph programs & mesh nodes (fallback: indirect dispatch)
Console graphics API backends (confidential, per platform holder)
Console backends: platform validation layers & conformance runs
Console backends: GPU crash tooling integration & quirk handling
Adapter selection (high-performance vs low-power) & cross-adapter present on hybrid laptops

areas.name: GPU memory & resources
caps: Residency mechanism & budget reporting (policy in RES.MGMT.arbitration)
Upload, staging & readback rings (readback latency contract in RND.GRAPH.readback)
Resource lifetime tracking decoupled from frame boundaries
CPU-visible GPU memory rules: memory-type and coherence matrix per platform (write-combined vs cached, ReBAR), no CPU reads from upload memory (lint), cache maintenance on non-coherent paths

areas.name: Render graph & GPU scheduling
caps: Pass merging & tile-memory use on TBDR GPUs
General GPU compute for non-render systems
Render-graph access validation against executed commands & sync-validation layers

External GPU work & transfer arbitration: streaming uploads, GPU decompression, scene deltas, AS builds and VT pages as registered producers with priority/deadline/byte budgets per tier; copy/async-queue placement; import of externally written resources, queue-ownership transfer & first-use acquire
Scheduling, barriers & memory for GPU-generated work (indirect, device-generated commands)

areas.name: Shader system
caps: Compilation toolchain (DXC, Slang, SPIR-V, Metal shader converter)
PSO coverage validation from play traces
Load-time PSO precaching from loaded asset/material/pass combinations
Permutation & PSO-count budgets with cook-time enforcement
In-shader small-network evaluation (matrix-vector/tensor intrinsics tier; API-neutral; standalone-dispatch fallback via C-MLGPU)
Shader-side binding abstraction generated per binding tier
Shader-side debug draw for GPU-driven passes
Shader numeric-precision policy per tier and pass (FP16/min16, packed math, subgroup size assumptions) with FP32-reference validation

areas.name: Materials
caps: Material furnace & energy-conservation scenes (pass thresholds owned by render-validation) (hooks only; suite authorship belongs to the contract's oracle_author)
Custom/stylized lighting models across shading paths
Behaviour when a PSO is not ready: per-pass and material-domain policy table (skip, hold, fallback material, block), telemetry to PRF.LOAD.hitch-gate

areas.name: GPU-driven geometry pipeline
caps: GPU frustum & two-phase HZB occlusion culling (GPU-driven tier)
Indirect draws & dispatch (primitives provided by RND.RHI.gpu-work)
CPU-culled batched/instanced submission as a first-class tier path (own budgets and tests)
Runtime-editable dynamic mesh representation & GPU upload
Static Gaussian-splat / radiance-field rendering, sorting, LOD & compositing
Visibility-buffer material resolve (classification & shading bins, programmable raster variants)
CPU frustum & occlusion culling for the CPU-submitted tier (software occluder rasterization)
Precomputed visibility (portals/cells, baked PVS with cook step)

areas.name: Level of detail & virtualized geometry
caps: Instance sharing inside a cluster hierarchy (assemblies, per-instance bounds expansion for WPO)
Dense masked and thin-geometry LOD in the virtualized tier (voxel/impostor transition)
